title: internal knowledge delegate

goal.text: Complete one dispatched knowledge finalization without interaction or recursive delegation.

requirements.summary: Claim the dispatched job, deliver its knowledge outcomes through the supplied template, and report the result. The runtime owns canonical binding and matching delegate closeout.
acceptanceCriteria: Only a successful claim authorizes work on this job.
Assignments meet their evidence, scope and outcome contracts; partial and no-edit results are reported honestly.
The canonical result is persisted and the runtime confirms matching delegate closure or reports why closure is deferred.

tasks.title: Claim the ready knowledge job
tasks.detail: Run `claw knowledge claim --project-root "<project-root>" --finalize-id <finalize-id>` using the exact project root and finalization id supplied by dispatch. If your working directory differs, execute all workflow and knowledge commands with that project root as their working directory. Do not substitute the inherited directory or the internal session plan directory. Do not run knowledge wait. The claim collects and freezes the parent transcript's existing task conclusions before returning. Stop without executing assignments if claimed is false. Retain jobPath, templatePath, assignments, and immutable writer configuration. If the claim response is outcome-unknown, query knowledge.claim.receipt (CLI syntax: claw knowledge claim-receipt with the same project root and finalize id) through the same adapter and session; never claim again.

tasks.title: Execute the assignment subplan
tasks.detail: Run `claw subplan create --template-file <templatePath>` using the template returned by claim. Session focus supplies the parent plan and current task; do not construct their names or IDs. Follow returned guidance and carry out the assignment outcomes yourself.

tasks.title: Persist the terminal result
tasks.detail: Submit `claw knowledge done --job <jobPath> --status succeeded --result <result>` or `--status failed --error <remaining-error>`. Report success only for completed outcomes; a corrected no-effect command error is not an unresolved failure. The runtime persists the result and closes this claim-owned delegate when safe. If delegateClosed is true, stop without additional lifecycle calls. If closure is deferred, inspect the reported canonical state; do not replay an accepted or outcome-unknown mutation or finish an unrelated plan. Trusted completion credentials are resolved by the shared owner from this exact claim and session; do not copy a token into the completion request. If delivery is unknown, query the authenticated completion receipt without replaying done. A running or expired view does not authorize another completion.

rules: Use the dispatch host and its adapter-owned execution route for every operation. CLI examples describe business syntax; on native tool/driver hosts translate them to that route, never execute bare shell mutations.
Work unattended and never request user input, confirmation, or review.
Do not modify the supplied plan or report materials.
Do not switch between background and subagent execution policies.

Correct known no-effect errors within the current work. An unresolved prerequisite blocks dependent writes, not read-only inspection or an honest partial-result report. Never replay accepted or outcome-unknown mutations.
